speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that background. To better understand your condition, could you tell me when you first noticed the gait instability and if it has been progressively worsening?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very serious finding; PML is typically caused by severe immunosuppression. Have you recently been taking immunosuppressive medications like natalizumab or rituximab, or have you been diagnosed with HIV? REQUEST TEST: CD4 Count and HIV Viral Load.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unexpected, as PML almost always occurs in the setting of significant immune deficiency. Given the normal HIV and CD4 counts, could you describe your current medication list or any recent cancer treatments like CAR-T cell therapy you might have received?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine and Lumbar Spine to rule out compressive myelopathy. Have you noticed any bladder or bowel dysfunction, such as retention or incontinence, which would suggest spinal cord involvement rather than PML?

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your MRI confirms PML despite normal immune markers, and you are experiencing asymmetric limb ataxia, have you recently started any new medications such as CAR-T cell therapy or had recent chemotherapy? Additionally, do you have any history of autoimmune disorders or recent infections that might explain this paradoxical presentation?

REQUEST TEST: CAR-T Therapy History and Recent Infection Panel.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical Spine and Lumbar Spine.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No recent CAR-T cell therapy or chemotherapy initiated. No history of autoimmune disorders or recent infections identified. MRI Cervical Spine and Lumbar Spine findings: No evidence of compressive myelopathy, disc herniation, or spinal cord lesions.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the confirmed PML lesions despite normal immune markers and no spinal pathology, have you ever used recreational drugs like IV drugs, or do you have a history of unexplained fevers and weight loss suggesting an underlying malignancy? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count and Comprehensive Metabolic Panel.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) with an occult immune-deficient state.
